title: 25 January–18 February - Berlin Conference, a meeting of the foreign ministers of the United States, Soviet Union, United Kingdom and France
text: The Berlin Conference of 1954 was a meeting of the "Big Four" foreign ministers of the United States, Britain (Anthony Eden), France (Georges Bidault), and the Soviet Union (Vyacheslav Molotov) from 25 January to 18 February 1954. title: 18–29 June - 4th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 4th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 18 to 29 June 1954. This year's festival did not give any official jury prizes, instead awards were given by audience voting.

title: Germany wins the 1954 FIFA World Cup Final in Association football
text: The final match of the 1954 FIFA World Cup was played at the Wankdorfstadion in Bern, Switzerland, on 4 July 1954, and saw West Germany beat the heavily favoured Golden Team of Hungary 3–2. Earlier in the group stage, Hungary had defeated West Germany 8–3.

title: Otto John, president of the West German Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution since 1950, having disappeared from the West, resurfaces in East Berlin and denounces Western policies. In December 1955, he returns to the West
text: Otto John was a German lawyer and intelligence official. During World War II, he was a conspirator in the 20 July plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler.

title: Wittig reaction reported. Georg Wittig shares the 1979 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for its discovery
text: The Wittig reaction or Wittig olefination is a chemical reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with a triphenyl phosphonium ylide called a Wittig reagent. Wittig reactions are most commonly used to convert aldehydes and ketones to alkenes.

title: 1954 Bitburg explosion: an explosion of military jet fuel kills 34
text: The devastating Bitburg tank explosion took place on 23 September 1954 at the then NATO air base near the city Bitburg, in the municipality of Niederstedem, Germany. The explosion took place in an underground storage tank containing JP-4, a military jet fuel blend.

title: Bonn–Paris conventions: treaties and protocols are signed in Paris, paving the way for West German rearmament and its admission to NATO (6 May 1955).
text: West German rearmament began in the decades after World War II. Fears of another rise of German militarism caused the new military to operate within an alliance framework, under NATO command. The events led to the establishment of the Bundeswehr, the West German military, in 1955.

title: 1954 East German general election (a sham election as East Germany is a one-party state)
text: General elections were held in East Germany on 17 October 1954. It was the second election to the Volkskammer, which had 466 deputies; due to the four-power status of the city of Berlin, the 66 deputies from East Berlin were indirectly appointed by the East Berlin magistrate.

title: The high-speed angle grinder is invented by Ackermann + Schmitt (FLEX-Elektrowerkzeuge GmbH) of Steinheim an der Murr
text: An angle grinder, also known as a side grinder or disc grinder, is a handheld power tool used for grinding, polishing, sanding, and similar applications. Its use is especially prevalent in metalwork.

title: The first electric drip brew coffeemaker is patented in Germany and named the Wigomat
text: Drip coffee is made by pouring hot water onto ground coffee beans, allowing it to brew while seeping through. There are several methods for doing this, including using a filter.
